extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, physicians, and members of the Royal Society (17th-century scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions and experimental reports across natural history, instruments, physiological diagnosis, and material testing (e.g., pulse interpretation, hygroscope design, bee comb handling, burning springs, and incombustible cloth). Contains observational criteria and protocols for assessing phenomena and artefacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes of pulse variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists probable causes of pulse variation: 'The climate, season, temperament, age, diet, passion, disease, &c.' and links pulse character to these factors (e.g., French pulse more equal and quick; higher/nearer the sun quicker; rainy seasons more free and nimble).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these factors when interpreting pulse changes: consider climate (altitude/latitude), season, individual temperament (melancholy, bilious, sanguine, phlegmatic), age (children small, old men uncertain), diet (gluttony, fasting), passions (fear, joy, anger), and presence/stage of fever or specific diseases (scorbutic, hysteric, icteric, hydropic, gout, plague). The author warns many remarks are speculative ('These are mere assertions') but presents them as a diagnostic checklist for correlating pulse features with states of body and mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pulse types and their diagnostic meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorizes pulses by time and strength and by quality: unequal in time or strength; interrupted; intense; remiss; superficial; deep; leaping; trembling; wandering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation guidance provided: unequal in time often in acute distempers and seldom very dangerous; unequal in strength (weaker/stronger) is dangerous and can precede death; 'interrupted' (strokes much smaller or intervals greater) shows decay of strength and may forerun swooning/palsies/apoplexies; 'intense' = very hard stroke or frequent small strokes (e.g., fever); 'remiss' = weaker strokes and more dangerous in sickness; 'superficial' indicates 'exact temperament' and merry mind; 'deep' indicates disposition to melancholy/asthma/lethargy and more in aged; 'leaping' often not dangerous; 'trembling' shows great extremity with poor recovery prospects; 'wandering' sometimes precedes dissolution. Use these descriptions as diagnostic signals and temporal warning signs (e.g., wandering pulse often precedes death by minutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hygroscope design and mechanism (Molyneux)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design: a whipcord (AB) ~4 feet tied at A with weight C at end that carries index D over a graduated circle on board EF; moisture twists the cord and moves the index; drying untwists it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction and operational guidance: tie cord at both ends but allow one end to twist under a suspended weight so moisture penetration shortens/twists the cord (analogy to a screw). Test by wetting/drying and by placing warm water vapour beneath to observe twist/untwist; even breathing produced measurable rotations ('8 or 10 breathings would twist it 5 degrees'). Note behavior under localized heat (candle/heated iron) and compare to oat-beard hygrometers. Address potential issues: cord may register more than one turn (inconvenient) and remedy by hanging at midpoint (G) to halve effective turns of the index. Observe and document sensitivity to small atmospheric changes (clouds, overshadowing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance and durability criteria for hygrometers
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualities contrasted with older hygrometers: sensitivity to small atmospheric changes, consistency over time, and resistance to weakening with age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A superior hygrometer 'obeying its alterations very nicely' should show immediate response even when 'not the least shower falling' and detect rising/vanishing clouds. Beware a common defect of former hygrometers: they 'grow weak with age' (planks/boards season, oat-beards perish). Long-term durability must be monitored over time to determine if the invention suffers the same fault. Instrument design should also record and manage multiple-turn registration to avoid ambiguous readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and extraction procedure for West Indies bottle-like honey-combs
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed combs composed of small bottle/bladder-shaped wax cells (brownish-black, like Spanish olives) clustered like grapes and typically lodged in hollow trees or rock cavities by the sea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling: when removing combs, carry them gently and maintain the same position they were in. Extraction: pierce every bottle with a thorn of a wild palm or a pin 'a little more than 1/2 from the bottom' — piercing lower risks sediment hindering the honey's running. Note honey characteristics: 'as clear and liquid as rock-water' and purgative if drunk fasting; observe storage and sanitary handling to preserve quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria/evidence for oviparity and species identification (macreuse vs bernacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards used to argue these sea-birds are oviparous and not generated from non-animal substrates: presence of reproductive anatomy suited for generation, laying of eggs, and observed breeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use direct anatomical examination, observations of egg-laying, and breeding records to classify whether a form is oviparous. The author rejects mythic equivocal generation accounts and stresses anatomy and observed life history (eggs and breeding) as decisive evidence when determining whether such creatures are birds (and to place them taxonomically among geese, ducks, colymbi, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical character (labyrinth/ampulla of trachea) as taxonomic/functional criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that some sea-ducks lack an ampulla (labyrinth) in the angle of the windpipe; presence/absence and structure vary among species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence, size, and structure of the tracheal ampulla ('labyrinth of the trachea') to investigate function (voice modulation vs air-reservoir) and as a comparative anatomical character for species identification. The text suggests surveying which birds have or lack it and whether it is present in males only or in females as well to infer function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of 'burning fountains' (boiling vs burning springs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Burning fountains described as actually cold at source yet inflammable and ignitable at a distance by a lighted body; distinct from boiling springs which do not take fire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When characterising such springs, observe phenomena at their source (flammability in situ), and test whether the waters/earths retain properties when removed (they often do not produce boiling/flaming when removed from source). Evaporate samples to detect residues (e.g., 'a dark or pitch-like substance') and record local health claims (e.g., curative mud, longevity) cautiously—these are reported observations requiring further verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental protocol and evaluation metrics for incombustible cloth
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol and observations used to test linen claimed to be incombustible: measure dimensions, weigh before and after trials, expose to oil and red-hot fire, and observe consumption, char, and any changes (mass lost, cleanliness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended tests and metrics: (1) measure size (length/breadth/fringe); (2) weigh precisely before trial and after (documenting losses: e.g., 'lost in the burning 2 drs. 5 grs.'); (3) subject samples to severe tests—oil poured on while red-hot, sustained exposure to clear charcoal fire for several minutes; (4) note whether cloth consumes, chars, or ignites nearby material (e.g., did not consume white paper laid on it when red-hot); (5) repeat experiments across settings (private/public trials, different institutions) and document reproducibility; (6) record qualitative observations (became 'a little whiter and cleaner' after burning). Consider historical testimonies but base claims on controlled empirical trials; report both results and weights to allow quantitative comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical features to distinguish true from false pregnancy (case indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case narrative lists observed features in a woman claiming seven years' gestation: abdominal tumefaction 'sursum, more gravidarum', episodic nausea/vomiting, appetite changes, perceived fetal motions (sensed by physician's hand over clothes), enlarged but not overly flaccid mammæ with distinct glands, regular urine, and overall preserved health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a combination of signs to evaluate pregnancy authenticity: distribution and character of abdominal swelling (hydropic vs gravid pattern), presence/quality of mammary gland enlargement, history of fetal-like motions (corroborated by examiner), systemic symptoms (nausea, vomiting, appetite), changes in urination, and absence/presence of other disease signs. Also consider functional tests (e.g., shift of bulk when patient lies on side — the patient denied perceiving weight shift) and repeated examinations over time. The narrative cautions that extraordinary durations and lack of corroborating evidence (and that opening the body was not permitted) complicate definitive judgment.
